outcome: Pelvic floor muscle strength (measured by perineometer)
finding: While women after vaginal delivery initially experienced more pelvic floor muscle weakness, prolapse, and distress, these symptoms improved over time, with similar questionnaire scores to the cesarean group at 6 months.
mod_finding: Women who had a vaginal delivery had greater pelvic floor muscle weakness, pelvic floor disorder symptoms, and prolapse severity compared to those who underwent cesarean section; however, these symptoms improved over time and were similar between the two groups at 6 months postpartum.
